title: Bram and the Asset
premise: Cyrus Dunmore, a disgraced intelligence analyst living under a new name in a coastal town, receives a call on a burner phone that was supposedly destroyed years ago—the voice belongs to Mara Voss, the partner they loved and lost when an operation went wrong. Mara is alive, embedded as an asset inside a trilateral covert program, and she's been feeding evidence of illegal renditions to someone who is now hunting her. As Cyrus races to extract her, they must outmaneuver an assassin named Kestrel, evade the three governments that burned them both, and decide whether justice means exposing the program or destroying it. In the end, Cyrus gets the truth to a journalist at devastating personal cost, Mara survives but walks away to protect them, and Cyrus finally stops running—choosing to testify openly rather than stay invisible.
about_author: C. M. Nystrom is the pen name of a former policy researcher who spent a decade writing about surveillance and accountability before turning to fiction. They live near the sea, where most of their thrillers are drafted in the off-season quiet of coastal towns.

chapters.title: The Phone That Shouldn't Ring
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Seven years into a quiet life repairing boats, Cyrus receives a call on a burner number they personally destroyed. The voice is Mara's—dead for seven years, officially. The emotional beat is vertigo: the careful walls of invisibility cracking open in a single ring.

chapters.title: Salt and Old Names
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Flashbacks interleave with Cyrus checking old tradecraft: who could have this number, and why now? A neighbor notices their agitation, reminding Cyrus how fragile belonging is. The beat is dread mixed with longing—they realize part of them never stopped waiting for this call.

chapters.title: What the Program Buried
chapters.summary: Mara's POV, via a recorded dead-drop audio. She explains she faked her death to infiltrate Meridian, a joint extraction program run by three governments, and has proof of unlawful renditions. The beat is cold clarity: she isn't asking Cyrus to rescue her; she's asking them to finish what they started.

chapters.title: Kestrel
chapters.summary: Assassin's POV. We meet Kestrel, methodical and eerily courteous, closing in on Mara's network from the other end. He finds one of her couriers dead. The beat is menace without melodrama—a professional doing homework, which makes him scarier than any fanatic.

chapters.title: Three Flags
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Cyrus travels to Rotterdam and contacts a former colleague, Odile, trading a favor for access to Meridian's shipping manifests. The numbers don't add up, confirming Mara. The beat is the old competence reawakening—and the fear that using it makes them visible again.

chapters.title: The Man Who Bounced Me
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Cyrus confronts Deputy Director Halloran, the man who ended their career, under cover of a routine records request. Halloran knows more than he should and warns them off with genuine regret. The beat is bitter recognition: the system isn't evil, it's self-protecting, which is worse.

chapters.title: Dead Drop in the Rain
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Cyrus retrieves Mara's physical evidence cache but spots a tail—Kestrel's advance work. A tense, wordless chase through a fish market ends with Cyrus escaping by using harbor knowledge Kestrel lacks. The beat is adrenaline and the first blood drawn in the story.

chapters.title: Rules I Rewrote
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Hiding in Odile's flat, Cyrus decrypts the cache and finds their own name in Meridian's files—not as victim but as designated scapegoat for the original operation. The beat is betrayal curdling into resolve: they were never paranoid; they were managed.

chapters.title: The Asset Speaks
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Inside Meridian, Mara faces an internal audit and must lie brilliantly to her own handlers while passing a final message to Cyrus. The beat is claustrophobic tension—she is safest exactly where she is most alone.

chapters.title: Odile's Price
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Odile agrees to help exfiltrate Mara but demands Cyrus hand over the evidence to her agency instead of the press. Cyrus stalls, lying to a friend for the first time since exile. The beat is moral erosion—justice outside the law requires betraying its gatekeepers.

chapters.title: Tea with the Assassin
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Kestrel corners Cyrus in a café, not to kill but to recruit: he's realized his employers intend to erase him too. He offers Mara's location and his silence—for a copy of everything. The beat is uneasy alliance; the enemy is more honest than the allies.

chapters.title: Harbor Lights
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Cyrus and Mara reunite briefly at a safehouse—seven years of grief compressed into one night that neither can afford. They plan the extraction and argue about whether exposure or destruction serves justice. The beat is love against duty, tender and doomed-feeling.

chapters.title: The Audit Turns
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Meridian's internal review flags Mara; her handler gives her one chance to prove loyalty by identifying the leak. She names a dead man and buys forty-eight hours. The beat is a countdown beginning, the clock now audible in every scene.

chapters.title: Halloran's Confession
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Halloran, facing retirement and conscience, meets Cyrus secretly and confirms the scapegoat order came from above all three agencies. He won't testify, but he gives them the name of a journalist with the files' verification keys. The beat is a door opening that can't be closed.

chapters.title: Extraction
chapters.summary: Multi-POV set piece. The planned extraction through a container port goes wrong when Meridian moves up Mara's transfer. Kestrel, honoring the deal, creates a diversion; Odile's team arrives uninvited. Cyrus pulls Mara out amid gunfire. The beat is chaos, sacrifice, and the alliance fraying even as it saves them.

chapters.title: What We Owe the Dead
chapters.summary: Cyrus and Mara alternating. Safe but cornered, they argue bitterly: Mara wants to vanish again together; Cyrus wants to publish. Old wounds reopen over who chose duty last time. The beat is the relationship's darkest hour—love tested not by danger but by disagreement.

chapters.title: Kestrel's Ledger
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Kestrel delivers his copy of the evidence to Cyrus, then disappears to settle his own accounts with Meridian. His final message reveals the program's leadership will convene in Prague within days. The beat is melancholy respect—an assassin choosing a kind of justice too.

chapters.title: Prague, Forty Hours
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Cyrus and Mara infiltrate the Meridian summit to plant verification beacons that will authenticate the files for the journalist and three oversight committees simultaneously. The beat is taut procedural suspense—every step rehearsed, every step capable of killing them.

chapters.title: The Room Where It Ends
chapters.summary: Climax, dual POV. Caught in the summit building, Mara surrenders herself to draw security while Cyrus reaches the server floor. Halloran, present for the summit, makes his choice and unlocks the door for them. The beat is sacrifice converging—everyone paying something for the truth.

chapters.title: Signal
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. The files go live worldwide as Cyrus escapes across rooftops with Kestrel's unexpected covering fire. Meridian's leadership scatters; arrests begin within hours. The beat is catharsis with cost—victory that feels like an ending and a beginning at once.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Instead of accepting a quiet deal and a new identity, Cyrus chooses public testimony before an oversight committee, naming themselves and their own complicity. Mara watches from the gallery. The beat is the theme fulfilled: justice outside the law ultimately demands standing inside it, exposed.

chapters.title: The Boat, Repaired
chapters.summary: Epilogue, Cyrus's POV. Months later, back at the harbor with a suspended sentence and a repaired boat, Cyrus finds Mara waiting on the dock—no longer an asset, no longer dead. They cast off together with no destination. The beat is belonging earned at last: home is a person, not a hiding place.
